correctness.rationale: Laguerre L² orthogonality gives the exact covariance 1/4 Li₂(|ρ|²). Stationarity yields the finite variance formula. The linear term integrates to 1/(4n) exactly by Parseval. After x=nθ substitution the nonlinear H=Li₂−identity has a uniform integrable second-order difference quotient, with O(x²(1+|log|x||)) near zero, O(x⁻²) for large x, and vanishing outside-domain tail; dominated convergence gives C/n+A/n³+o(n⁻³), with A>0. Exact finite n=1,2 cases and 21 independent checker assertions corroborate. No limiting distribution is claimed.

value.rationale: The logarithmic Mahler measure is the log-geometric mean of the modulus and a classical zero-sensitive statistic. Its random Gaussian fluctuations have a natural 1/n scale; the result determines the leading and first nonzero higher asymptotic constants, and proves a nontrivial cancellation of the entire 1/n² correction. The positive n⁻³ coefficient distinguishes finite polynomial length from the limiting sinc-process approximation and provides a precise calibration benchmark rather than a routine expectation formula.
